the ion-ion neutralization of He2+ and C6F6– in the helium afterglow produces the He2(C,D, E, F, c, d, e, f) states in the 19.22–20.62 e V range, which is very similar to the product distribution obtained from the He+/C6 F6 – ion-molecule reaction.
the ion-ion neutralization reactions of He2+ and He+ with C6H6− and C6F6– in the He flowing afterglows have been investigated.
the He2(C,D,F,c,d,e) and He2(E) states were formed in the He2+ / C6F6– reaction in a He flow afterglow.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the formation of He2(C,D) and He2(E,F) states by the reaction of He2+/C60− and He+/ C60− in the helium flowing afterglow and the formation of the He2(C,D,F) states in the He2+/ C6F6 reaction.
the ionization processes of He2+ and He+, and the subsequent formation of He2* and the excited states of He*.
the formation of the He2(C,D,F,c,d,e) states by the He2+/CH4− reaction in the helium flowing afterglow, and the He2(E) state by the He2+ + CH4 reaction in a pulsed helium afterglow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
He2(C,D,F) and He2(e,f) states were produced from He2+/C− and He+/F− reactions, respectively.
the He2+ ion is not the primary source of the observed He2(C,D,F) states.
the He2+ + C6F6 − → He2 + C6F5 + F reaction is the dominant reaction pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionization potential of He2 is 19.82 ± 0.02 eV.
the He2(C,D) and He2(E,F) states in this reaction have a similar product state distribution as the He2* and the He* states in the He+/C6 F6− reaction.
the He2(C,D) and He2(E,F) states are produced by He2+/C2F4−, He2+/C5F8−, and He2+/C7F14−, while He2(c,d,e,f) are produced by He+/C2F2−, He+/C2Cl4−, He+/CF2Cl2−, He2+ and He+/C5F10−, and He+/C7F16−.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ion-ion neutralization reactions can be a powerful tool for producing the excited He2* and the metastable He* states in the energy ranges of 19.2-20.6 eV and 19.8-21.2 eV, respectively, which have not been accessible by the conventional methods.

the He2+ + C6F6 − → He2* + C6F5 + F reaction proceeds via a direct charge transfer mechanism, and that He2* is formed in the same electronic states as He2+ is formed in the He2+/He− ion-ion recombination reaction.
the He2+ ion can be regarded as a source of He2*.
